newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stoiber aide calls for CSU-CDU talks on euro.
newsitem.headline: Stoiber aide calls for CSU-CDU talks on euro.

text.p: Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber on Friday called for "clarifying meeting" with Chancellor Helmut Kohl to discuss differences over the path towards European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Stoiber, a leading member of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) which is a junior partner in Kohl's ruling coalition, has urged delaying monetary union unless all would-be participants meet the strict fiscal targets.
Kohl and Stoiber are scheduled to appear at a CSU event in Munich next week, but the chancellor has already said he would not meet the Bavarian premier at the event.
Stoiber's spokesman in the Bavarian state government said that "Such fundamental questions cannot be discussed on the sidelines of some event at which Edmund Stoiber and Helmut Kohl appear together."
Instead, Stoiber would like to discuss the issue with Kohl at the next routine strategy meeting of the CSU and CDU, which is scheduled to take place in September.

The mass daily Bild newspaper reported on Friday that Stoiber has threatened to block European monetary union by voting against launching it in the upper house of parliament, or the Bundesrat, which must give final approval to Germany's participation in EMU.
The Bavarian government spokesman called the report "speculation", but would neither confirm nor deny its substance.
